title: Memorizing Long-tail Data Can Help Generalization Through Composition
claim: Error on both common and rare features falls as the data-scaling parameter grows, and noise raises error most on rare features.
layout: 4 line-plot panels in a row, shared x-axis α, one legend
description: A single row of four line plots, each with α on the x-axis from 1.0 to 4.0. Each plot has four curves for noise levels σ = 0, 0.05, 0.5 and 1, colored from dark purple to bright green. The legend sits in panel (d). Panel (a) plots average estimation error on common features, with math notation in the title. Panel (b) plots average error on long-tail features. Panel (c) plots in-distribution test loss. Panel (d) plots out-of-distribution test loss. In every panel, error drops steeply from α=1 to 1.5 and then flattens. High-noise curves stay clearly above the low-noise ones, and the gap is largest in the long-tail and out-of-distribution panels. The eye goes first to the steep green curves at the top left of each plot. Panel captions are printed in large serif text below the plots.
caption: (a)(b) Average Error on Common and Long-tail Features on Linear Model; (c)(d) In- and Out-of-Distribution Test Loss on Linear Model
abstract: Deep learning has led researchers to rethink the relationship between memorization and generalization. In many settings, memorization does not hurt generalization due to implicit regularization and may help by memorizing long-tailed examples. In this paper, we consider the synergy between memorization and simple composition -- the ability to make correct prediction on a combination of long-tailed features. Theoretically, we show that for a linear setting, memorization together with composition can help the model make correct predictions on rare test examples that require a combination of long-tailed features, even if such combinations were never observed in the training data. Experiments on neural network architecture on simple data show that the theoretical insight extends beyond the linear setting, and we further observe that the composition capability of the model depends on its architecture.
